To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermoelectric performance of BixSb1.8-xTe3 alloys prepared by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintered can be improved by optimizing the Bi:Sb ratio.
the thermoelectric properties of Bi x Sb 2−x Te 3 can be improved by optimizing the composition.
the power factor and ZT value of BixSb(2−x)Te(3) alloys can be improved by controlling the ratio of Bi to Sb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the Bi–Sb–Te system for p-type thermoelectrics.
a new approach to optimizing thermoelectric properties by compositional optimization in the BixSb(2−x)Te3 system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bi0.3 Sb1.7 Te3 alloy has a better thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) at temperatures below 423 K, and Bi0.5 Sb1.5 Te3 is a better choice for temperatures above 423 K.
Bi0.3-xSb1.8+xTe3 is a better candidate than Bi0.5-xSb1+xTe3 for p-type thermoelectrics at room temperatures.
Bi0.3−0.5SbxTe1.7−1.5 (x = 0.2–0.46) alloys with SiC nanoparticles are promising p-type thermoelectrics for near-room-temperature applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZT values of the Bi1−xSb1+xTe3 alloys can be enhanced by optimizing the composition, especially for the alloys with low x values.

the Bi0.3–0.5SbxTe3 alloys with 0.1 wt.% SiC nanoparticles exhibit better thermoelectric performance than those with the conventional composition of 0.5Bi–1.5Sb–1.5Te, and Bi0.3−xSb1.4+xTe3 (x ≤ 0.1) is the best choice.

the ZT values of p-type Bi-Sb-Te alloys can be improved by optimizing the compositions of Bi and Sb, and the MA-SPS method is an effective way to fabricate high-quality Bi-Sb- Te bulk alloys.
